evidence_quotes.agenda: Never asked — call started as an availability inquiry, went straight into logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: 'I just wanna make sure I'm like locked in before I buy flights.' Rep: 'Yes, you are locked in. I've got you on the schedule.' — fully resolved a real anxiety (flying in from Colorado) before moving on.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'That is loosely an estimate obviously. I don't know how many items you have... that's why we'll give you the lower range to the higher range and then you have us for as long as you need, but you also only pay for as long as we are there.'

top_strength: Handled a genuinely anxious out-of-state customer (flying in just for the move) with real reassurance on both estimate accuracy and booking security — textbook Save Your Ass 'window' explanation delivered naturally.
coaching_note: No quid pro quo framing or agenda question at all — this was a rich, detail-heavy call where a proper agenda ask up front could have surfaced the lock-in and estimate-accuracy anxieties earlier and more directly.
grading_notes: No unusual judgment calls — this is a straightforward full sales call graded on its face.
